title: Dynamic priority-based telemetry reshaper for low-latency console metrics
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: The current ingest pipeline occasionally experiences head-of-line blocking during short spikes of high-cardinality console events (per-token cost attribution, route-level traces). This leads to increased p99 ingestion latency and downstream aggregation lag for critical dashboards. Existing fanout processors do not apply tenant-aware QoS or dynamically reorder messages based on urgency.

Goal: Implement a 'telemetry reshaper' service placed between the ingress gateway and the enrichment/aggregation layer that implements dynamic priority admission, lightweight reshaping (repartitioning and TTL-based promotion), and backpressure-aware shedding to keep p99 ingest < 300ms and end-to-end console dashboard freshness < 30s under 3x baseline load. The reshaper must preserve at-least-once delivery semantics and integrate with our schema registry and tracing.

Scope: design and implement a streaming microservice that consumes from the primary ingress topic, applies tenant+route QoS scoring, enforces priority-aware enqueuing into downstream topics, supports configurable emergency shedding policies, and exposes observability for queue depth, per-priority latency, and dropped event counts. MVP does not require exactly-once semantics or full stateful windowing; those are follow-ups.

Out-of-scope: reworking the enrichment processors, changing storage backends, or adding new client-side SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Reshaper service deployed behind feature flag and consuming from ingress topic without data loss for 24h during canary
Under 3x synthetic spike traffic, ingest p99 measured at reshaper output <= 300ms for priority=high and <= 800ms for priority=low
Dashboards indicate end-to-end console metric freshness (ingest -> deck aggregators) < 30s for 95% of tenants during spikes
Configurable policies (per-tenant priority weights, TTL promotion rules, shedding thresholds) available in Console and respected by service
Comprehensive tracing: each reshaped event contains reshaper decision and priority tag; traces link back to incoming request id
Automated integration test that replays production sampling with priority labels and verifies no silent drops when shedding disabled
technical_design:
Architecture: Kafka (ingress topic) -> telemetry-reshaper (consumer group) -> priority output topics (ingest-high, ingest-medium, ingest-low) -> downstream enrichers. The reshaper is implemented as a horizontally scalable stateless cluster with an optional local in-memory bounded priority buffer per instance.

QoS scoring: score = base_tenant_weight * route_factor + realtime_boost + error_penalty. Tenant weights are read from a central config service; route_factor derived from route metadata in the event. Realtime boost used for events tagged as 'interactive' (Console UI traces).

Admission control: accept if buffer occupancy < soft_limit for priority band, otherwise try to re-route to overflow topic (cold-path) or apply TTL-based promotion for time-sensitive events. Shedding occurs only when global memory pressure > high_watermark and low-priority events exceed TTL.

Repartitioning strategy: for hot tenants we support on-the-fly partition hinting by adding a tenant_shard header so downstream consumers can do affinity processing; we will not change topic partitions at runtime.

Durability & semantics: use Kafka offsets + consumer group commits. At-least-once semantics guaranteed by committing only after successful publish to downstream topic. Future work: introduce idempotent producer and transactional writes for exactly-once.

Observability: metrics (Prometheus) per-priority: input_rate, output_rate, queue_size, retries, dropped_count. Tracing: span for reshaper decision and output publish. Logs: structured JSON with decision_reason.

Config: central feature-flag gate, per-tenant weights stored in ConfigDB, policy expressed as YAML and editable in Console with validation.

Scaling: horizontal autoscaling on output lag and queue_size; add a warm-up ring buffer during scale-ups to minimize head-of-line impact.
implementation_tasks: Spec: finalize scoring formula and policy knobs (Aisha, 2d)
Library: shared priority buffer implementation in go-lib-queue (Connor, 3d)
Service: implement telemetry-reshaper service (Connor + backend eng, 6d)
Config: ConfigDB schema + Console UI for tenant weights and policies (PM+Frontend, 4d)
Tests: integration test harness that replays sampled production topic and verifies SLA (SRE, 5d)
Deploy: feature-flagged canary (10% initial traffic) followed by 50% then 100% (DevOps, 3d)
Docs: runbook + troubleshooting + SLOs in Confluence (On-call, 2d)
risks_mitigations: Risk: incorrect scoring causes unfair shedding for a tenant -> Mitigation: add dry-run mode that logs decisions and exposes per-tenant impact dashboard before shedding enabled
Risk: increased producer latency due to extra hop -> Mitigation: co-locate reshaper in same AZ and tune producer acks to async when safe
Risk: priority buffer OOM on burst -> Mitigation: bounded buffers, circuit-breaker to overflow topic and alerting
Risk: schema drift in events -> Mitigation: integrate with schema registry and reject malformed events with metric and dead-letter topic
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal traffic only, feature-flag enabled for infra team (1 week)
Canary: 10% of ingress traffic for non-critical tenants, monitor p99 and dropped_count (72h)
Ramp: 50% traffic for all tenants with warning thresholds enabled (48h)
GA: 100% traffic and Console policy UI enabled for SRE/PM to tune (monitor for 2 weeks)
Fallback: toggle off feature flag to drain buffers and switch traffic back to previous topic if > 4x baseline errors
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring and policy parsing
Load tests: synthetic spike harness using k6 + Kafka producer to simulate 5x baseline
Chaos tests: broker partitioning and consumer restart during canary
Integration: end-to-end test validating trace propagation and offset commit behavior
SLO validation: synthetic test that asserts dashboard freshness under spike
